title: Avalanche’s Nathan MacKinnon out a month, Cale Makar out 2 weeks due to injuries
content:
The Colorado Avalanche won’t have their two superstar players available against the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday, nor for the foreseeable future.

Forward Nathan MacKinnon will miss a month and defenseman Cale Makar will miss the next two weeks after both players suffered lower-body injuries against the Ottawa Senators on Thursday, Avalanche head coach Jared Bednar confirmed to the media Saturday. While MacKinnon’s injury wasn’t specified, Bednar said Makar had played through a “soft tissue” injury that worsened in Ottawa.

Makar and MacKinnon suffered injuries within seconds of each other during the second period of Colorado’s 4-3 overtime loss at Canadian Tire Centre. Makar appeared to be in pain while collecting a loose puck in the offensive zone, forcing him to leave the game. He then returned for one more shift in the second period. Moments later, MacKinnon fell to the ice and held his hip after being cross-checked by Senators defenseman Artem Zub. Neither MacKinnon nor Makar appeared in the third period.

“They’re two of the best players in the world,” Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog said after the game. “So you’d like to have them, no doubt. But I don’t think it’s any different, right? You play with whoever you’ve got, whoever’s ready to go, whoever’s healthy and up. They play. So, (I) hope those guys will be just fine.”

MacKinnon has 10 goals and ranks fifth in points among NHL players this season with 30, trailing Edmonton’s Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl, Kirill Kaprizov and Evan Bouchard. Makar has five goals and 23 points in 19 games this season.
